mcpInstall.prompt1: Connect to my Cortex account (my exam revision app).
mcpInstall.prompt2: It is a remote MCP server: address {url}, Streamable HTTP transport, OAuth 2.1 sign-in (I’ll sign in to Cortex in my browser and authorise access; there is no API key to enter).
mcpInstall.prompt3: If you can add an MCP server yourself, add it under the name “{name}”. Otherwise, tell me exactly where to add it in your app.
mcpInstall.prompt4: Once connected, call the list_courses tool to check that you can see my courses.
mcpInstall.prompt5: Before using any paid tool (mock exam, practice question, marking or course preparation), tell me its credit cost and wait for my approval.
mcpInstall.claude1: In Claude (web or desktop), open Settings → Connectors, then “Add custom connector”.
mcpInstall.claude3: Leave the OAuth identity fields (Client ID and Client Secret) blank: Claude registers itself.
mcpInstall.claude4: Click “Connect”: the Cortex page opens. Choose what Claude can do, then click “Authorise”.
mcpInstall.claudeNote: On mobile, first add the connector from the web or desktop app; it will then appear in the mobile app. On Team and Enterprise plans, an administrator adds it in the organisation settings.
mcpInstall.chatgpt1: Open the ChatGPT plugins page, click +, then “Add custom MCP server”.
mcpInstall.chatgpt2: Name: Cortex. Under Connection, paste the MCP server URL:
mcpInstall.chatgpt3: Authentication: OAuth. Read the warning, click “I understand and want to continue”, then “Create as a plugin”.
mcpInstall.chatgpt4: ChatGPT opens the Cortex page: choose what it can do, then click “Authorise”.
mcpInstall.chatgptNote: Depending on your ChatGPT plan and workspace policies, adding a custom MCP server may not be available.
mcpInstall.claudeCode2: Then type /mcp in Claude Code, choose cortex and “Authenticate”: your browser opens the Cortex page.
mcpInstall.cursor1: Install in one click (Cursor must be installed):
mcpInstall.cursor3: On first use, Cursor opens the Cortex page in your browser: authorise access.
mcpInstall.vscode2: Or open the command palette, choose “MCP: Add Server” → HTTP, then paste the address. From the command line:
mcpInstall.vscode3: VS Code asks you to sign in to Cortex when starting the server: authorise access.
mcpInstall.thenLogin: Then sign in (your browser opens the Cortex page):
mcpInstall.gemini2: Then sign in from Gemini CLI:
mcpInstall.geminiNote: Google does not document adding a custom MCP server to the consumer Gemini app; use Gemini CLI.
mcpInstall.other1: Add a remote server (HTTP, “Streamable HTTP”) with this address:
mcpInstall.other2: Authentication: OAuth, with no key or ID to enter; the client registers itself with Cortex.
mcpInstall.other3: Most common configuration format (the address field may be called url, serverUrl or httpUrl):
mcpInstall.otherNote: A client that only supports local servers (stdio) cannot connect directly to Cortex.
